---
title: "Compare spatial samples using biological replicates"
---

Spatial observations, sections and biological subjects are different levels of
replication. Keep their identities explicit before comparing conditions.
`SpatialSampleSummary()` accepts either a Seurat object or a cell metadata table;
label-only imaging data need no invented expression matrix.

## Cell-type or domain composition

Assume the metadata contains `celltype`, `sample`, `patient` and `condition`.
Each sample/section must belong to exactly one patient and one condition.

```r
summary <- SpatialSampleSummary(
  object, group.by = "celltype", sample.by = "sample",
  subject.by = "patient", condition.by = "condition"
)
comparison <- SpatialSampleComparison(
  summary, contrast = c("Control", "Treatment"), paired = FALSE
)
comparison$comparisons
SpatialSamplePlot(comparison)
```

The order of `contrast` is explicit: effects are Treatment minus Control.
Composition denominators are all labelled observations within a sample. A
missing cell-type category has zero count; missing cell-type labels are rejected.
For Visium, these are fractions of labelled spots, not deconvolved cell counts.

Repeated sections are first averaged equally within patient and condition, and
the patient means enter Welch's t test. The confidence interval refers to the
mean difference in fraction units. BH correction covers all testable rows of the
call. This simple two-group analysis does not adjust covariates or model
compositional dependence, and does not establish a causal effect. Use an
appropriate dedicated model when those assumptions are needed.

## Paired and insufficiently replicated designs

```r
paired_comparison <- SpatialSampleComparison(
  summary, contrast = c("Before", "After"), paired = TRUE
)
paired_comparison$subject_values
paired_comparison$comparisons
```

Paired inference uses complete patient pairs, after section aggregation. The
number of excluded unpaired subjects is returned for each feature. The plot
shows the underlying subject values. An independent contrast rejects subjects
present in both conditions. Fewer than two subjects per group or two complete
pairs yields `not_tested`, with a reason and missing p/FDR. Undefined standard
error also produces `not_tested`. It never substitutes a test across individual
cells. Two replicates are a computational minimum, not a study-design target.

## Neighborhood composition

First compute neighborhoods separately for each sample/image using
`SpatialNeighborhoodProfile()`. Preserve the complete surrounding tissue while
selecting target cells. For pooled metadata-only objects, always supply
`sample.by` so identical coordinates in different sections cannot create edges.

```r
profile <- SpatialNeighborhoodProfile(
  object, group.by = "celltype", sample.by = "sample",
  radii = c(25, 50), cells = target_cells
)
summary <- SpatialSampleSummary(
  object, group.by = "celltype", sample.by = "sample",
  subject.by = "patient", condition.by = "condition", profile = profile
)
comparison <- SpatialSampleComparison(summary, c("Control", "Treatment"))
SpatialSamplePlot(comparison)
```

For a multi-image object, pass an image explicitly to each profiling call and
combine their tables with `rbind`; do not silently use the first image. The
summary validates that each profile cell and sample agrees with the design.
Distance intervals must share compatible coordinate units before combination.

Each sample estimate is the mean fraction across its evaluable target cells,
giving each target equal weight. Empty neighborhoods retain NA, and a sample
with no evaluable target observations remains missing. These are observed
fractions, not spatially corrected enrichment scores or ligand-receptor
probabilities. Preserve the source/parameter attributes when exporting results.

## Outputs and reproducibility

```r
saveRDS(comparison, "spatial-subject-comparison.rds")
write.csv(comparison$sample_values, "spatial-sample-values.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(comparison$subject_values, "spatial-subject-values.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(comparison$comparisons, "spatial-comparisons.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

The saved RDS retains design provenance and statistical parameters. The CSVs
separate sample measurements, subject means and inferential results. A plot can
be rebuilt from the saved comparison without running any backend again.
